report.source_text: A CT of the abdomen and pelvis with triple (intravenous, oral and rectal) contrast was done, which revealed multiple fairly defined hypodense, peripherally enhancing nodular foci of different sizes in the bilateral psoas muscles, both gluteal muscle groups, paravertebral and bilateral proximal medial thigh muscles. The largest of these, measuring 3.3×1.6×1.3 cm with an approximate volume of 6.9 cc, was noted in the right psoas muscle. There was a slight diffuse thickening of the gastric fundus and sigmoid colonic walls (figure 1). There were noted hypodense nodules at the liver, right adrenal gland and spleen. Enlarged lymph nodes with necrotic centres were noted in the left iliac and superficial inguinal regions. A well-defined 0.7 cm partially exophytic, thinly septated hypodense cystic focus is seen in the cortex of the superior pole of the right kidney. Pericardial thickening, worrisome for metastasis, was appreciated. Subcutaneous fat stranding was noted in the anterolateral chest wall and in the right and left flank muscles also. Multiple fairly to well-defined areas of lysis were noted in the sacrum, bilateral iliac, right ischium, proximal femurs, and some of the posterior elements and bodies of the visualised vertebrae. An ill-defined enhancing isodense mass lesion measuring 3.0×3.2 cm is noted at the right parahilar region.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old non-smoker with no prior gastrointestinal disease history presented with a 3-month progressive non-productive cough, upper back pain, and facial/upper extremity swelling with neck vein engorgement, consistent with superior vena cava syndrome. Physical examination confirmed distended neck veins, prominent superficial vessels, decreased breath sounds and vocal fremitus at the right lung base, and upper extremity swelling (BP 180/100, HR 85, RR 19, O2 sat 98%). CT chest revealed a 3.4×3.5×2.7 cm mass at the right lower lung with atelectasis and perilesional ground glass densities, and a 3.7×4.3×4.5 cm heterogeneous mass in the right paratracheal region with mass effect, along with a prominent carinal lymph node with calcification and multiple subcentimeter cervical and axillary lymph nodes. CT abdomen/pelvis demonstrated diffuse thickening of the gastric fundus and sigmoid colonic walls, extensive metastatic disease including bilateral psoas and gluteal muscle metastases, hypodense nodules in the liver, right adrenal gland, and spleen, enlarged necrotic lymph nodes in the left iliac and superficial inguinal regions, pericardial thickening, and multiple areas of bone lysis in the sacrum, bilateral iliac bones, right ischium, proximal femurs, and vertebrae. Bronchial alveolar lavage cytology showed atypical cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and pleomorphism, with characteristic signet-ring cells demonstrating mucin inclusions pushing the nucleus to the periphery. Immunohistochemical panel (CK-7, CK-20, TTF-1, calretinin) was consistent with metastatic disease of gastric or pancreaticobiliary origin. The case was signed out as metastatic adenocarcinoma with signet-ring features. The patient subsequently received radiation therapy (400 cGy daily for 3 days) with noted improvement of symptoms, along with supportive medical management including blood pressure control and dexamethasone for dyspnea relief.

CT chest revealed a 3.4×3.5×2.7 cm mass at the right lower lung with atelectasis and perilesional ground glass densities, and a 3.7×4.3×4.5 cm heterogeneous mass in the right paratracheal region with mass effect, along with a prominent carinal lymph node with calcification and multiple subcentimeter cervical and axillary lymph nodes. CT abdomen/pelvis demonstrated diffuse thickening of the gastric fundus and sigmoid colonic walls, extensive metastatic disease including bilateral psoas and gluteal muscle metastases, hypodense nodules in the liver, right adrenal gland, and spleen, enlarged necrotic lymph nodes in the left iliac and superficial inguinal regions, pericardial thickening, and multiple areas of bone lysis in the sacrum, bilateral iliac bones, right ischium, proximal femurs, and vertebrae. Bronchial alveolar lavage cytology showed atypical cells with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and pleomorphism, with characteristic signet-ring cells demonstrating mucin inclusions pushing the nucleus to the periphery. Immunohistochemical panel (CK-7, CK-20, TTF-1, calretinin) was consistent with metastatic disease of gastric or pancreaticobiliary origin. The case was signed out as metastatic adenocarcinoma with signet-ring features. The patient subsequently received radiation therapy (400 cGy daily for 3 days) with noted improvement of symptoms, along with supportive medical management including blood pressure control and dexamethasone for dyspnea relief.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Clinical presentation of superior vena cava syndrome with progressive respiratory symptoms
Imaging evidence of right paratracheal mass (3.7×4.3×4.5 cm) with mass effect and right lower lung mass (3.4×3.5×2.7 cm) with atelectasis
Bronchial alveolar lavage cytology showing signet-ring cells with mucin inclusions pushing nucleus to periphery, consistent with adenocarcinoma
Pathology signed out as metastatic adenocarcinoma with signet-ring features
Extensive metastatic disease on CT abdomen/pelvis including gastric fundus thickening, muscle metastases, hepatic/adrenal/splenic nodules, bone lysis, and pericardial thickening
Immunohistochemical panel (CK-7, CK-20, TTF-1, calretinin) consistent with gastric or pancreaticobiliary origin
Treatment response to radiation therapy with symptom improvement

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: TTF-1 negative immunostaining and signet-ring cell morphology more consistent with gastric origin; imaging shows paratracheal mass compressing lung rather than primary lung lesion
CT abdomen/pelvis shows gastric fundus thickening and sigmoid colonic wall thickening; immunostaining consistent with gastric or pancreaticobiliary origin, but gastric wall involvement more prominent

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Benign pleural effusion or inflammatory process
